title: Customers Still Subscribed
statement:
The billing database holds `customer(id, name, country)` and `subscription(id, customer_id, plan, status)`. A subscription's status is `active`, `cancelled`, or `paused`.

Write one query returning the `name` of every customer with at least one `active` subscription, in alphabetical order. Each name must appear once; a `cancelled` or `paused` subscription does not count.
sql_schema:
create table customer (id int primary key, name text not null, country text not null);
create table subscription (id int primary key, customer_id int not null references customer(id), plan text not null, status text not null);
sql_seed:
insert into customer (id, name, country) values (1, 'Ada', 'GB'), (2, 'Grace', 'US'), (3, 'Linus', 'FI'), (4, 'Barbara', 'US');
insert into subscription (id, customer_id, plan, status) values (1, 1, 'pro', 'active'), (2, 2, 'team', 'cancelled'), (3, 3, 'pro', 'active'), (4, 4, 'free', 'active'), (5, 1, 'team', 'cancelled'), (6, 2, 'pro', 'paused');

reference_solutions.source: select distinct c.name from customer c join subscription s on s.customer_id = c.id where s.status = 'active' order by c.name

test_cases.input:
insert into customer (id, name, country) values (5, 'Ken', 'US');
insert into subscription (id, customer_id, plan, status) values (20, 5, 'pro', 'active');

insert into customer (id, name, country) values (6, 'Zoe', 'NL'), (7, 'Aaron', 'IE');
insert into subscription (id, customer_id, plan, status) values (21, 6, 'pro', 'active'), (22, 7, 'team', 'active');
update subscription set status = 'cancelled' where customer_id in (1, 3);
insert into subscription (id, customer_id, plan, status) values (23, 1, 'enterprise', 'active');

update subscription set status = 'paused' where customer_id = 4;
update subscription set status = 'active' where id = 6;

title: Best Sellers by Quantity
statement:
An order database holds `product(id, name)` and `order_item(id, product_id, quantity)`.

Write one query returning the three products with the largest total quantity sold, as two columns: the product `name` and the total quantity. Order by total quantity descending, then by name ascending. Products that were never ordered do not appear.
sql_schema:
create table product (id int primary key, name text not null);
create table order_item (id int primary key, product_id int not null references product(id), quantity int not null);
sql_seed:
insert into product (id, name) values (1, 'Anvil'), (2, 'Bolt'), (3, 'Clamp'), (4, 'Drill'), (5, 'Ember');
insert into order_item (id, product_id, quantity) values (1, 1, 5), (2, 2, 12), (3, 3, 7), (4, 1, 3), (5, 2, 1), (6, 4, 7);

reference_solutions.source:
select p.name, sum(i.quantity)::int as sold
from product p join order_item i on i.product_id = p.id
group by p.name
order by sold desc, p.name asc
limit 3

test_cases.input: insert into order_item (id, product_id, quantity) values (7, 5, 100);
delete from order_item where product_id in (2, 4);
insert into order_item (id, product_id, quantity) values (8, 4, 1);

title: Reporting Depth
statement:
An org chart is stored as `employee(id, name, manager_id)`, where a null `manager_id` marks someone at the top.

Write one query returning every employee's `name` and how many managers sit above them: `0` for the top of a chain, `1` for their direct reports, and so on. Any order is accepted.
sql_schema: create table employee (id int primary key, name text not null, manager_id int references employee(id));
sql_seed: insert into employee (id, name, manager_id) values (1, 'Root', null), (2, 'Ada', 1), (3, 'Grace', 1), (4, 'Linus', 2), (5, 'Barbara', 4);

reference_solutions.source:
with recursive chain as (
  select id, name, 0 as depth from employee where manager_id is null
  union all
  select e.id, e.name, c.depth + 1 from employee e join chain c on e.manager_id = c.id
)
select name, depth from chain

test_cases.input: insert into employee (id, name, manager_id) values (6, 'Ken', null);
test_cases.expected:

Ken	0
Ada	1
Grace	1
Linus	2
Barbara	3
